Application Materials.content:
Please provide a CV. If your qualification is below 2:1 or in an unrelated subject, you are required to complete a personal statement for entry to this programme: [Urban Analytics Statement](https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_815260_smxx.docx).
As part of your online application, you also need to submit the following supporting documents:
- A copy (or copies) of your official degree certificate(s) (if you have already completed your degree)
- A copy (or copies) of your official academic transcript(s), showing full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained
- Official English translations of the certificate(s) and transcript(s)
- One reference letter on headed paper
- Evidence of your English language ability (if your first language is not English)
- Any additional documents required for this programme (see Entry requirements for this programme)
- A copy of the photo page of your passport
You have **42 days** to submit your application once you begin the process. You may save and return to your application as many times as you wish to update information, complete sections or upload supporting documents such as your final transcript or your language test.
**Reference:** Please provide one reference. This should typically be an academic reference but in cases where this is not possible then a reference from a current employer may be accepted instead. If you already have a copy of a reference on letter headed paper then please upload this to your application. If you do not already have a reference to upload then please enter your referee’s name and contact details on the online application and we will contact your referee directly.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Standard entry requirements: **2.1 Hons (or non-UK equivalent)** in Geography, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, Public Health, Economics, or a related Social Science subject, along with an interest in acquiring skills in data science, statistics, GIS, and spatial analytics.
- The University may also accept degrees in other disciplines such as Statistics, Information Science, Data Science and Engineering.
- The University may sometimes accept degrees at **2.2 Hons or non-UK equivalent**. Relevant, full-time work experience may also be considered.
- China-specific entry requirements: **Bachelor degree at 70%/75%/80%/85%/87%** depending on university attended, see Result Required 2.1 on the [China University Grade Equivalences List](https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_1221495_smxx.pdf), in Geography, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, Public Health, Economics, or a related Social Science subject, along with an interest in acquiring skills in data science, statistics, GIS, and spatial analytics.
- China-specific lower/alternative consideration: The University may sometimes accept **Bachelor degree at 65%/70%/75%/80%/85%** depending on university attended, see Result Required 2.2 on the [China University Grade Equivalences List](https://www.gla.ac.uk/media/Media_1221495_smxx.pdf).

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For applicants from non-English speaking countries, as defined by the [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english), the University sets a minimum English Language proficiency level.
- International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic and Academic Online (not General Training): **6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. IELTS One Skill Retake Accepted. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome), tests taken up to 20 January 2026: **90 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 20; Listening 19; Speaking 19; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome), tests taken from 21 January 2026: **92 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 22; Listening 20; Speaking 23; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- Pearsons PTE Academic: **65 overall** with no subtest less than Reading 60; Listening 60; Speaking 65; Writing 60. Online PTE not accepted for entry. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- Cambridge Proficiency in English (CPE) and Cambridge Advanced English (CAE): **176 overall with no subtest less than 169**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- Oxford English Test: **7 overall with no subtest less than 6**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- LanguageCert Academic/ Academic Online: **70 overall with no subtest less than 65**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- Password Skills Plus: **6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- Trinity College Integrated Skills in English II: **Two subtests at 96 or higher, and two subtests at 80 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- Kaplan Test of English: **Any two subtests at 480 or higher, and any two subtests at 450 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- University of Glasgow Pre-sessional courses: tests are accepted for **2 years** following date of successful completion.
Alternatives to English Language qualification:
- Degree from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have studied for a minimum of their final year at Undergraduate level, or 9 months at Master's level, and must have completed their degree in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
- Undergraduate 2+2 and 3+1 degrees from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have completed their final year of study in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
For international students, the Home Office has confirmed that the University can choose to use these tests to make its own assessment of English language ability for visa applications to degree level programmes. The University is also able to accept UKVI approved Secure English Language Tests (SELT) but does not require a specific UKVI SELT for degree level programmes. The University therefore still accepts any of the English tests listed for admission to this programme.
The University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from the English for Academic Study Unit Pre-sessional courses. Pre-sessional courses give direct entry to your University programme for successful students (no need to take IELTS). More information on [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/). The University can also consider the pre-sessional courses accredited by the below BALEAP approved institutions to meet the language requirements for admission to postgraduate taught degrees: Heriot Watt; Kingston Upon Thames; Middlesex University; Manchester University; Reading University; Edinburgh University; ST Andrews University; UCL; Durham.
As part of the online application, applicants need to submit evidence of English language ability if their first language is not English. In the application form’s English Language Proficiency section, applicants should state the date of any English language test taken (or to be taken) and the award date (or expected award date if known).

Program Overview.content:
The Urban Analytics MSc provides knowledge and skills to design and conduct appropriate analyses, with experience working with cutting-edge datasets and exposure to emerging tools, including those driven by artificial intelligence (AI). It is taught at the [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/) and is available as **12 months full-time** or **24 months part-time**. Academic contacts include [Dr Michael Sinclair](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/socialpolitical/staff/michaelsinclair/) and [socpol-student-recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk](mailto:socpol-student-recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk).
The programme provides a critical appreciation of the potential for big data and urban analytics, including AI-driven methods, to inform urban planning and policy making, as well as an understanding of practical and ethical limitations. It offers hands-on experience with statistical and GIS software and programming tools used to capture, process and analyse data. Students are exposed to cutting-edge datasets typically encountered by urban analysts and learn to apply analytical methods, from traditional statistical approaches to emerging AI techniques, to extract insights and address real-world urban challenges. The programme also develops students’ ability to convey results of complex data analyses in ways that have impact on policy makers and public debates.
Students benefit from the programme’s strong connection with the [Urban Big Data Centre](https://www.ubdc.ac.uk/) (UBDC), Glasgow’s world-leading urban analytics centre of expertise, and from close work with [the Data Lab](https://www.thedatalab.com/), an internationally leading research and innovation centre in data science. Students may have opportunities to visit [Aalto University](https://www.aalto.fi/en) in Helsinki, Finland under a funded academic exchange programme through the UK Turing Scheme, dependent on yearly funding success.
The programme structure includes five core and two to four optional courses, plus a research-based dissertation. Knowledge-focused courses introduce the context for urban planning and policy making, while skills-focused courses on statistical methods, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and programming provide opportunities to use a variety of real-world datasets. Courses are delivered via a mix of lectures, tutorials, supervised computing lab sessions and small group work. A wide range of optional courses allows students to pursue personal interests and enhance particular skills or domain-specific knowledge such as transport studies or urban design.
Career opportunities for graduates include positions in government agencies, urban planning organisations, city governments, public health boards, retail businesses, real estate companies, transport, and other private consulting firms. Alumni have also gone on to work in non-profit organisations and to be accepted into highly competitive PhD programmes in the UK, Europe, USA, and China, ranging from government, universities and technology companies.
The programme offers frequent connection with industry. It has strong links with the Urban Big Data Centre (UBDC), a research centre and national data service based at the University of Glasgow, and a vast majority of academic staff teaching on the MSc programme are involved with the centre. Students are regularly invited to join the CUSP London Data Dives, applying their learning in a fast-paced environment to improve understanding of real-world data science and develop skills in formulating questions, analysing data and presenting results. All students are eligible for the Data Lab Academy and have access to paid internships through the Data Lab.

Curriculum.content:
- **Teaching start:** September
- [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/)
- **MSc:** 12 months full-time; 24 months part-time
You will take five core and two to four optional courses, as well as submit a research-based dissertation. Knowledge-focused courses introduce you to the context for urban planning and policy making. Skills-focused courses on statistical methods, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and programming will give the opportunity to use a variety of real world datasets. Courses are delivered via a mix of lectures, tutorials, supervised computing lab sessions and small group work.

- [Programming Tools for Urban Analytics](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5123)

Optional courses:
- [Advanced Topics for Urban Analytics](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5160)
- [Digital Planning Systems and Tools](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5144)
- [Fundamentals of Transport Studies](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5101)
- [Smart Cities and Infrastructure](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5151)
- [Sustainable Urban Futures (10)](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5116)*
- [Statistical Methods for Transport Planning](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5103)

Dissertation:
- [MSc Dissertation Project (Urban Studies)](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/urbananalytics/?card=course&code=URBAN5080P)
*Programme structure is currently under review. Proposed changes for September 2026 entry include making Urban Analytics Group Project a core course and Sustainable Urban Futures an optional course. All changes are subject to approval.

Multiple Applications.content:
- Parallel applications to multiple programmes will be dealt with as separate applications at all times.
- Applicants must make a new application for each programme they want to be considered for.
- Applicants may accept more than one conditional offer but can only accept one unconditional offer.
- For some programmes, an application fee of **£25** may be charged.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
It may be possible to defer your offer to the next available intake. Deferral requests will be considered individually and are not guaranteed.
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake are open. To be considered for a deferral, you must have accepted a conditional or unconditional offer for the 2027 intake and have paid any relevant deposits to secure your place on the course. The deadline for requesting a deferral to the 2027 intake is **30 September 2026**. If you do not meet these criteria, your request will declined.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
You can apply for a postgraduate taught programme if you have not yet finished your first degree. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you finishing your degree at the required grade. If you are made a conditional offer, then you should upload your final results (transcript and degree certificate) when you recieve them.
You can normally apply for a programme if you have not yet met the English language requirements. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you meeting the English language requirements by the date stated on your offer letter. Please note a few exceptions to the rule where an English test is required at time of application exist. Please check the programme page for details.
If you cannot provide all the required documents when you apply, it is still possible to apply, but you must include in your application:
- a full current transcript (and an English translation if required)
The university may then be able to make you a conditional offer. You can then upload the remaining documents at a later date. Please note: some programmes require all the listed documents before a decision can be made.
